sections.overview: The Sphingidae Taxonomic Inventory accepts Hyles costata as a valid hawk-moth species.
sections.identification: The Amur account gives a 64–75 mm wingspan, pale forewing bands and a reddish hindwing field.
sections.habitat: In Amur it occupies dry meadows and steppe.
sections.diet: Euphorbia is reported as a larval host in Amur.
sections.behavior: Adults fly at dusk and night; Amur records span mid-June to early August.
sections.reproduction: Two annual generations are reported in Amur.
sections.ecology: Its taxonomic history includes treatment as a form of H. euphorbiae, but the specialist inventory records its reinstatement as a distinct species in 1993.
sections.conservation: The regional Red Book notes low local numbers and habitat loss.

sources.title: Steppe hawk-moth — Red Book of Amur Oblast
